_note: Single source of truth for every number in the Stage 1 submission. Nulls and empty lists fail the gates, so nothing here survives as a placeholder, and a string in a numeric field fails too. Week 2 fills geometry, operating, performance, efficiency, the candidate and sensitivity tables, power_by_radius, mass_envelope_g and sources. Week 3 fills pitch, pitch_schedule, vector_map and packaging. Week 4 fills structure, mass_budget_g and the remaining results. Hard limits are checked against values RECOMPUTED from geometry and the mass lines, so an optimistic headline number achieves nothing. mass_envelope_g lines are {item, nominal_g, conservative_g, basis, scaling_class} with distinct item names. mass_budget_g lines are {item, mass_g, conservative_g, basis, refines}, where refines names the mass_envelope_g item this line came from, so week 4 continuity is checked per component and not only on the total, and conservative_g is what builds results.mass_g_conservative rather than a growth rate chosen after seeing the target. See D33. Aerodynamic power is bounded below by momentum theory over the declared momentum_area_m2, which may not exceed 2R times span, and the figure of merit that falls out has to be credible for a cyclorotor. thrust_sensitivity freezes in week 2 what raising thrust costs, and week 4 may only choose a row from it. Structural demands are derived: per-blade mass from the blade budget and blade count, rotor shaft torque from shaft power and speed, blade root bending from thrust per blade, lever arm and load factor. Row shapes for the remaining lists, so nothing sits in the schema without one: configuration_candidates {config, rotors, module_mass_g, thrust_N, module_tw, selected}, 3 or more; coefficient_scenarios {name, blade_area_coeff, basis, evidence_class}, 3 or more, where evidence_class is measured, derived or downside and a transferred value is never called measured, and a measured row also declares solidity and chord_to_radius so the gate can test whether it was taken on this design's own shape family; aero_azimuthal_loads {azimuth_deg, normal_force_N}, 24 or more; drive_candidates {name, continuous_power_W, continuous_torque_Nm, mass_g, selected}, 2 or more; linkage_dimensions {link, length_mm}, 4 or more; pitch_schedule {azimuth_deg, pitch_deg}, 24 or more; vector_map {phase_command_deg, vertical_force_N, lateral_force_N}, 3 or more. Every mass_envelope_g line also carries scaling_class, one of geometry, power or fixed, because the drive is not a fixed mass.

configuration_candidates.config: two rotors, 3 blades each, 80 mm radius
three rotors, 3 blades each, 65 mm radius

coefficient_scenarios.name: K19 optimum rotor, measured on this shape family
coefficient_scenarios.basis: Kellen 2019, Table 2.1 configuration 8, printed p.17: 5.5 in chord, 3 blades, 8.25 in radius, 22 in span, NACA 0020, pitch amplitude 40 degrees. CT/sigma read off the vector path data of Fig 3.25 (1.04424) and Fig 3.28 (1.04428), which agree to 0.003 percent, then converted by coeff = (2/pi)(CT/sigma) out of Kellen's projected area convention A = span times 2R. Measured on Kellen's rotor and not on ours, and that rotor's solidity and chord to radius sit within 1.1 percent of this design's. Chord Reynolds 186,000, inside the 100,000 to 300,000 band that also contains this design's 134,074

coefficient_scenarios.name: S2 quad rotor hover point, corrected against the primary source
coefficient_scenarios.basis: Benedict 2010 printed p.236: at the operating RPM of 1800, each rotor produced around 1.91 N of thrust. Printed p.225 gives the same point as 195 grams at 1800 rpm and 40 degrees pitching amplitude. Four NACA 0010 blades of 33.0 mm chord and 158.8 mm span at 76.2 mm radius, printed p.220 and p.233. Recomputed in this project's blade area convention. This is the transfer the nominal should have rested on, and its chord Reynolds is 31,600 rather than the 35,100 the ledger carried

coefficient_scenarios.name: nominal, held at 0.6055 rather than raised
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the value the rest of the design is built on. Its arithmetic used 1.98 N at 2000 rpm, which is the 809 gram all-up vehicle weight of Benedict's Table 5.1 divided by four, paired with the twin rotor's operating speed. The source states neither as a quad thrust. All three measured or corrected points now sit above 0.6055, so the old error ran in the safe direction and the gap is held as deliberate margin rather than spent. See D36

coefficient_scenarios.name: S2 twin rotor, three blades at the same radius and speed
coefficient_scenarios.basis: 1.47 N per rotor, half of the 300 grams total Benedict 2010 printed p.229 reports at 2000 rpm, on three blades of 25.4 mm chord and 152.4 mm span at 76.2 mm radius, recomputed the same way. The source rounds the same quantity to 1.5 N per rotor on printed p.232. Higher than the quad but at a solidity of 0.159, far outside the measured band, so it is carried as an upside indication and not adopted

coefficient_scenarios.name: blade deflection loss only
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the nominal less a 5 percent thrust loss for blade bending and torsion, sized against the computed section stiffness rather than assumed. This is the low coefficient the conservative case now runs on, because the Kellen measurement retired the other allowance. See D35

coefficient_scenarios.name: deflection loss and configuration transfer, retired
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the nominal less 5 percent for blade flexibility and a further 10 percent for a transfer that changed blade count, airfoil and chord ratio at once with nothing measured to de-risk it. Retired on 31 August 2026 when Kellen came in at 0.6648, measured on this design's own shape family and above the nominal, which is the test D23 set. Kept as the record of what the conservative case used to be

pitch.mechanism: passive cyclic four-bar, one per blade, sharing a common offset pivot

linkage_dimensions.link: L1 rotor arm, rotor axis to blade pitch axis
linkage_dimensions.role: input crank, frozen by the week 2 radius

linkage_dimensions.link: L2 offset link, rotor axis to offset pivot
linkage_dimensions.role: ground link, its length sets the amplitude and its direction the phase

linkage_dimensions.link: L3 pitch link, offset pivot to horn tip
linkage_dimensions.role: output crank, scaled 9.133/9 off Kellen's built vehicle

linkage_dimensions.link: L4 pitch horn, blade pitch axis to link pin
linkage_dimensions.role: coupler, scaled 2/9 off Kellen's built vehicle

linkage_dimensions.link: pitch link closest approach to the rotor axis
linkage_dimensions.role: keep-out, nothing on the axis may sit in the pitch plane

linkage_dimensions.link: pitch link closest approach to a neighbouring pitch axis
linkage_dimensions.role: clearance against the next blade's root fitting

mass_envelope_g.basis: PMI foam core at 52 kg/m3 filling 88 percent of the NACA 0020 section, two plies of 60 gsm carbon twill skin at 0.22 kg/m2 over a 2.05 chord perimeter, a CFRP spar tube of 0.12 chord diameter and 0.5 mm wall, bond line and two root fittings, times three blades. Every dimension is assumed, so the conservative column takes the 20 percent structural rate
six CFRP spider arms of 14 by 1.5 mm section and radius length, two aluminium hub bosses and six blade attachment brackets. Assumed sections, 20 percent

two miniature pitch bearings and one CFRP pitch link with rod ends per blade, plus an aluminium offset ring of 6 by 3 mm section on the rotor radius with its two support bearings and three pivots. Assumed sections, 20 percent

CFRP through shaft of 14 mm diameter and 1 mm wall over the span, two steel stub adapters, and a drive end allowance of 18 g per newton metre of rotor torque. Length follows the span and diameter follows the torque, so the line is torque scaled and takes the 20 percent structural rate
two deep groove main bearings at the rotor stations, catalogue mass, bore sized on the shaft the rotor torque sets. Catalogue rate, 15 percent

two bearing blocks, four CFRP frame tubes of 8 mm diameter and 1 mm wall spanning the rotor envelope, a motor mount plate and four airframe mount lugs. Assumed sections on the least developed part of the module, 25 percent

T-Motor Antigravity MN5006 KV450, 650 W and 26 A maximum for 180 s from the supplier datasheet, derated by 0.80 for continuous duty to 520 W and 20.8 A, 106 g including leads. Catalogue rate, 15 percent

single stage HTD toothed belt reduction of 6 to 1: motor pulley, belt and tensioner hardware, with the rotor pulley rim mass following the torque it carries at 22 g per newton metre. Part catalogue and part assumed, 20 percent
one brushless controller rated above the motor 25 A continuous current, from the same catalogue class as the motor. Catalogue rate, 15 percent

two digital metal gear servos of the 12.5 g class driving the pitch offset direction. Servo torque follows the residual pitch link load, which follows thrust across the sensitivity table, so the line is power scaled and not fixed
one controller board driving the pitch offset servos. The only line in the envelope whose mass genuinely does not move with radius, thrust or torque
silicone power and signal wiring routed over the module envelope, so its length follows the largest dimension and the line is geometry scaled rather than fixed

screws, threaded inserts, standoffs and structural adhesive at the frame, bearing and blade attachment joints. Count and bond area follow the frame, so the line is geometry scaled. Assumed, 25 percent

performance.blade_area_coeff: Benedict 2010, quad-cyclocopter rotor at hover. The repository carried 1.98 N per rotor at 2000 rpm, a pair the source never states: printed p.236 gives 1.91 N at 1800 rpm and printed p.225 gives 195 grams at the same speed, and those recompute to 0.7211 in this convention. 0.6055 is held anyway per D36, so nothing downstream moves upward on a correction. Derived, never measured on this configuration
performance.blade_area_coeff_low: The nominal less the 5 percent blade deflection allowance and nothing else. The 10 percent configuration-transfer allowance retired when Kellen 2019 came in at 0.6648, measured on this shape family and above the nominal, which is the test D23 set. Still an engineering downside scenario rather than a published lower bound. See D35
performance.momentum_area_m2: Projected frontal area 2R times span, the standard cyclorotor momentum closure and the cap the gate applies
performance.power_loading_ref_N_per_W: Benedict 2010 twin-cyclorotor at its operating point, printed p.232: at the operating thrust of 1.5 N (per rotor), the power loading of the rotor was 0.062 N/W. The quad reaches 0.076 N/W on printed p.236, so 0.062 is the lower of the two measured routes and it is the one used
performance.blade_deflection_thrust_loss: Bounded from above by the computed blade section, not derived from it: EI 66.8 Nm2 gives 0.086 mm of tip deflection and GJ 9.6 Nm2 gives 0.054 degrees of twist, so the section alone supports well under 1 percent. The 5 percent is carried as a floor over build tolerance, bond line variation and unsteady effects the section does not model
performance.figure_of_merit: Kellen 2019 section 3.3, read off the thesis rather than a summary: the peak figure of merit was found to be 0.6, on a 3-bladed cyclorotor with a 5.5in chord, 22in. span, and 8.25 in radius. Reading CT/sigma off Fig 3.25 and CP/sigma off Fig 3.26 for that rotor and closing FM = CT^1.5/(sqrt(2)*CP) gives 0.595, so the stated value reproduces to 0.8 percent
performance.reynolds: 134,074 at the design point, inside the 100,000 to 300,000 band Kellen measured this shape family across, and Kellen's own optimum rotor sits at 186,000. The 100,000 ceiling D25 rested on comes from Shrestha and Benedict and still bounds the Benedict-derived nominal, but the shape family now carries a measured coefficient bracketing the design point. See D37

efficiency.transmission: Single stage toothed belt at 0.93. Assumed, not measured. Published belt drive efficiency runs 0.95 to 0.98 at these speeds, so this is on the pessimistic side of the range
efficiency.motor: Outrunner at 0.84. Assumed, not measured, and the sensitivity matters: at 0.78 the motor input rises to 552 W and the selected drive is at its rating
efficiency.esc: Brushless controller at 0.95. Assumed, not measured, and the least sensitive link in the chain

drive.continuous_rating: T-Motor publishes Max. Power (180s) and Peak Current (180s), which is a three minute maximum and not an indefinite hover rating. Week 2 derates both by 0.80 for continuous duty. The derate is a judgement, stated rather than hidden, because the problem statement gives no endurance requirement to size it against
drive.belt_ratio: Smallest ratio at which motor torque stays inside the derated continuous torque and motor speed stays under 90 percent of what the 6S pack can turn it at, allowing for the internal resistance drop at the working current

thrust_sensitivity.drive_consequence: MN5006 KV450 at 2.5 to 1 covers it with the most room of any row, 12.65 A of the 20.8 A continuous
MN5006 KV450 at 3.5 to 1, 17.27 A of the 20.8 A continuous
MN5006 KV450 at 3.5 to 1, 20.61 A of the 20.8 A continuous and 8417 of 9435 motor rpm. The design point, and the tightest row that still fits

no shortlist drive fits at this radius. The motor input of 512.6 W is inside the 520 W continuous, but the torque wants a belt ratio the KV450 cannot spin to on 6S, which is why raising thrust stops paying here
